title: Best Dehumidifier for Cockroaches (2026): Cut Off Their Water
dek: Roaches can go weeks without food but not long without water. Drying the damp spots they depend on is one of the smartest moves in any roach plan.
description: The best dehumidifier for cockroaches in basements, crawl spaces and apartments — and why drainage matters, plus the steps that actually end a roach problem.
intro: Cockroaches are tough, but they have a weak spot: water. Entomologists commonly note that a roach can survive around a month without food but only about a week without water, which is why you find them near sinks, tubs, floor drains and damp basements. So it makes sense to ask whether a **dehumidifier for cockroaches** — or a dehumidifier for roaches in the basement — can help.

It can, with an important caveat. Lower humidity makes basements, crawl spaces, bathrooms and laundry rooms much less inviting, especially to moisture-loving species like the American and Oriental cockroach. But a dehumidifier won't eliminate an established infestation, and a German cockroach colony in the kitchen will keep going as long as it has crumbs and a dripping faucet. Think of a dehumidifier as one part of a plan that also includes sanitation, sealing and baits.

There's also a twist few guides mention: a dehumidifier bucket full of water is itself a roach water source. That's why every pick here can drain continuously, or holds its moisture where pests can't reach it.

blocks.text: Exact survival times vary by species and temperature, but the pattern holds: water is the resource roaches can least afford to lose. Humid air on its own isn't drinking water, but damp basements and bathrooms come with condensation, leaks and wet surfaces — and those are what a dry, ventilated space takes away.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for cockroaches

blocks.text: We don't lab-test dehumidifiers. We compare capacity ratings under the 2019 DOE test procedure, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals and CPSC recall records, then read owner reviews for patterns such as failing pumps or leaking tanks.

For roaches, we added a rule most dehumidifier guides don't need: **no standing water**. Every pick either pumps or hoses condensate away, or holds moisture in a desiccant. We then matched units to the places roaches gather — basements, crawl spaces, apartments and sink cabinets.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier for roaches

items.label: A pump or hose, not a bucket
items.text: Continuous drainage removes a ready water supply. If you must use a bucket, empty and rinse it daily.

items.label: The right capacity
items.text: 50 pints for a damp basement, 20–35 for a bathroom, laundry room or apartment. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) covers the details.

items.label: A set-point humidistat
items.text: Set 45–50% and let the unit cycle. Lower isn't better and wastes power.

items.label: Easy-to-clean parts
items.text: A washable filter and a tank you can scrub keep the unit from collecting grime pests like. Our [dehumidifier maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) has a schedule.

items.label: Placement off the floor where possible
items.text: A unit on a block or shelf is easier to clean around and leaves fewer hidden, warm corners.

sections.heading: A complete plan: dehumidifier plus these steps

items: **Fix every leak.** Dripping faucets, sweating pipes, a loose dishwasher drain and a leaky toilet tank are all roach water sources.
**Dry the sink cabinets.** Clear them out, wipe them down and leave the doors open for a day after any leak repair.
**Clean up food.** Store dry goods in sealed containers, wipe counters nightly and don't leave pet food out overnight.
**Seal gaps.** Caulk around pipes entering walls, behind appliances and along baseboards. Add door sweeps and repair torn screens.
**Use baits, not just sprays.** Gel baits and bait stations placed along the routes roaches travel tend to reach the hidden colony.
**Run exhaust fans.** Use the bath fan during and about 20 minutes after showers, and a vented range hood when cooking.
**Run the dehumidifier.** Keep basements, crawl spaces and laundry rooms at 45–50%, and confirm it with a hygrometer.

blocks.title: A note on allergies
blocks.text: Cockroach droppings and body parts are a well-documented indoor allergen and asthma trigger. If anyone in your home has asthma, a professional treatment plan is worth it — see our [best dehumidifier for allergies](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-allergies/) guide for the humidity side.

A dehumidifier won't end a roach infestation alone, but it removes the damp conditions that let moisture-loving species settle in. For most basements, the **GE APER50LZ** is the one to buy, because its pump means there's no bucket of water for pests to find. Choose the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** for a crawl space, the **Midea Cube 35** for an apartment, and an **Eva-Dry E-333** for the cabinet under the sink. Seeing centipedes too? They hunt roaches — our [best dehumidifier for centipedes](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-centipedes/) guide covers both.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier get rid of cockroaches?
faqs.a: Not by itself. A dehumidifier makes damp areas less appealing, especially to American and Oriental cockroaches, but an active infestation also needs sanitation, sealed entry points, baits and often a pest professional.

Yes. Most cockroaches gather where moisture is easy to find — basements, bathrooms, laundry rooms and under sinks. Lowering humidity and fixing leaks removes one of the main things keeping them there.
The bucket can. A tank of standing water is a ready drink for pests. Use a pump or hose to drain continuously, or empty and rinse the bucket every day.
Keep basements, bathrooms and laundry rooms around 45–50%. That's inside the EPA's recommended 30–50% range for homes and discourages mold, silverfish and centipedes too.

faqs.q: Should I use a dehumidifier for roaches in the kitchen?
faqs.a: Usually it isn't the main fix there. Kitchen roaches, typically German cockroaches, are driven by food and leaks. Clean thoroughly, repair drips, use baits and run the range hood. Save the dehumidifier for damp basements and laundry rooms.

faqs.q: Are water bugs the same as cockroaches?
faqs.a: In everyday speech, "water bug" usually means the Oriental cockroach or the large American cockroach, both of which favor damp places. A dehumidifier is especially helpful against these moisture-loving species.
